review: The print gives stanza 1 as a two-line acclamation and stanzas 2–4 as four lines; the payload follows the print, so `hebrew-meter.mjs` reports the shape 2/4/4/4 as irregular by construction.
1:1 מְאֹד נִשְׂגָּב — 'greatly exalted'; the Arabic قَدْ فَاقَ مَجْدُهُ is 'His glory surpassed', and Hebrew states the exaltation rather than the comparison so the line ends on a strong word.
2:4 הִתְגַּלְּמָה הַשְּׁלֵמוּת — 'perfection took shape', for تَجَسَّمَ الْكَمَال; the hithpa'el of גלם is post-biblical, but it is the standard verb for incarnation and avoids the ambiguous בשר.
3:2 מִי וִתֵּר כְּבוֹדוֹ — Philippians 2:7 (הִפְשִׁיט אֶת־עַצְמוֹ); the Arabic مَنْ ضَحَّى بِالْمَجْدِ is the same self-emptying, and וִתֵּר is the liturgical verb for yielding a right.
3:4 חַי כְּעֶבֶד נִבְזֶה — 'He lived as a despised slave' (Phil 2:7, צוּרַת עֶבֶד); the Arabic قَدْ عَاشَ كَالْعَبْدِ is that verse.
